e.etymology: A recent Indian name, popular with Hindu families in India and the US. Name sites gloss it in different ways and no single Sanskrit derivation is established.
Created for Princess Azula, the fire-bending antagonist of the animated series Avatar: The Last Airbender (2005). The name echoes azul, Spanish for blue, the color of her flames.
namesakes: Azula (fire-bending princess of Avatar: The Last Airbender)

assoc.t: villain princess of Avatar: The Last Airbender

e.note: Azula is the show's ruthless villain, so fans will catch the reference at once.

e.meaning: from the Asante people of Ghana
e.etymology: From the Ashanti, or Asante, people and former kingdom of Ghana. It came into American use in the 1970s as an African heritage name and peaked in 2002 with the singer Ashanti.

assoc.t: Ashanti people and historic kingdom of Ghana

e.etymology: From Hawaiian lani, sky or heaven, also used of royalty. It is the short form of the many Hawaiian names ending in -lani, such as Leilani and Kalani.
A variant of Melania, from Greek melaina, dark, the source of Melanie, with the sound of Milan and Milana. It was made familiar by Milania Giudice of The Real Housewives of New Jersey.

assoc.t: first lady Melania Trump, a near sound-alike

e.etymology: From an English surname and place name, originally Kirkby, from Old Norse kirkja, church, and byr, settlement: a village with a church.
namesakes: Kirby Puckett (Hall of Fame Minnesota Twins outfielder)

assoc.t: Kirby, Nintendo's round pink video game hero

e.meaning: member of the Gauts, a Germanic tribe
e.etymology: A modern spelling of Jocelyn, from Old French Joscelin, a Germanic name built on the tribal name Gaut, a Geat or Goth. It was a man's name in medieval England.
From the English word star, Old English steorra, sometimes first a nickname. It joined Stella, from the Latin word for star, as a girls' name in the 20th century.
namesakes: Star Jones (lawyer and former co-host of The View)

assoc.t: star, the celestial body, and a word for a celebrity

e.meaning: an Irish form of Mary; also Greek for fate
e.etymology: Anglicized from Irish Máire, the Irish form of Mary. By coincidence, moira is also the Greek word for fate; the Moirai were the three Fates.
namesakes: Moira Rose (Catherine O'Hara's matriarch on Schitt's Creek)
Moira Kelly (actress in The Cutting Edge and voice of Nala)

assoc.t: Moira Rose, the Schitt's Creek matriarch

e.etymology: A respelling of Cyrus, the Greek and Latin form of Old Persian Kurush, a name of uncertain meaning. Cyrus the Great founded the Persian Empire in the 6th century BC.
A spelling of Hadassah, from Hebrew hadas, myrtle. In the Book of Esther it is the Hebrew name of Queen Esther.
From the Spanish word brisa, breeze. It is also used as a short form of Briseida, the Spanish form of Briseis from the Iliad.
Mostly a spelling of Kayla, favored in Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking families. It is also close to Keilah, a town in the Hebrew Bible, and to the Yiddish name Kaila.
An elaboration of Amber with the -ly ending of Kimberly and Beverly. Amber, the golden fossil resin, takes its name from Arabic anbar. Amberley is also an English place name.
From an English surname meaning son of Jenyn, a medieval pet form of John. Its 1890s peak as a first name followed the presidential run of William Jennings Bryan.

assoc.t: country outlaw Waylon Jennings (as a surname)

e.etymology: From Arabic Asma, usually derived from a root meaning high or exalted. Asma bint Abi Bakr, daughter of the first caliph, was an early companion of Muhammad.
e.note: Asma is the Spanish, Portuguese and Italian word for asthma, and sounds close to it in English.

e.etymology: A spelling of Elijah that follows the Hebrew Eliyahu, my God is Yahweh, the name of the Old Testament prophet. For girls it is also used as an Aaliyah-style respelling.

A respelling of Nevaeh, the word heaven written backward, which took off after singer Sonny Sandoval of P.O.D. gave it to his daughter in 2000. With the vowels switched, Naveah no longer reverses to heaven.
e.note: Nevaeh is heaven backward; this spelling is not, so expect to correct people.

e.etymology: A spelling of Alistair, the anglicized form of Scottish Gaelic Alasdair, which is Alexander: Greek alexo, to defend, and aner, man.
An elaboration of Eliana used mainly in Dominican and other Caribbean Latino families, where names ending in -anny are popular. Eliana is Hebrew for my God has answered.
From an English surname and the word blithe, Old English for merry or cheerful. Several English rivers and towns are named Blythe or Blyth.
namesakes: Blythe Danner (actress and mother of Gwyneth Paltrow)

e.etymology: A modern American name in the family of Daylin, Dalen and Jaelyn, combining the Day- sound with the -lyn ending. It has no older meaning of its own.
The Arabic form of Solomon, from Hebrew Shlomo, built on shalom, peace. In the Quran Sulaiman is a prophet and king famed for his wisdom.

e.meaning: from Conwy, the Welsh river and town
e.etymology: From a surname taken from Conwy, the river and walled town in North Wales, and also from several Irish surnames anglicized as Conway.
namesakes: Conway Twitty (country singer of Hello Darlin')

e.etymology: The Latin spelling of Greek daimon, a guiding spirit, and the source of the word demon. As a name it doubles as a spelling of Damon, and it rose after Prince Daemon Targaryen in HBO's House of the Dragon (2022).

assoc.t: Prince Daemon Targaryen of HBO's House of the Dragon
daemon, an old spelling of demon

e.note: Many people will read it as demon; daemon is the older spelling of that word.

e.etymology: Recorded as a surname; as a first name it was made familiar by Mexican actress Eiza González, known from telenovelas and the film Baby Driver.
namesakes: Eiza González (Mexican actress in Baby Driver and Ambulance)

e.etymology: A pet form of Michael, built from the short form Mick plus the -ey ending. Michael is Hebrew Mikha'el, 'who is like God?'. Mickey has also been used for girls named Michaela or Michelle.
namesakes: Mickey Mantle (Yankees Hall of Fame slugger)

assoc.t: Mickey, Toni Basil's 1982 cheerleader pop hit
a mickey, a secretly drugged drink

e.note: Mickey Mouse comes to mind first, and 'mickey mouse' is slang for something trivial or amateurish.

e.etymology: From Hebrew Tzuriel, joining tzur, 'rock', and El, 'God'. In the Book of Numbers, Zuriel son of Abihail is the chief of the Merarite clans of the Levites.
From Arabic marw, a hard white stone such as flint or quartz. Al-Marwa is one of the two hills in Mecca that pilgrims walk between during the Hajj, the other being Al-Safa.

assoc.t: Al-Marwa, hill in Mecca walked to during the Hajj

e.etymology: Usually taken as a spelling of Charis, from Greek kharis, 'grace, kindness', a word used throughout the New Testament. Some parents use it as a form of the Welsh name Carys, 'love'.
The Catalan form of George, from Latin Georgius and Greek Georgios, from georgos, 'farmer'. Saint George (Sant Jordi) is the patron of Catalonia. In English it can also be a pet form of Jordan.
From Arabic karam, 'generosity, noble character', from the same root as Karim. It is also a given name in Punjabi Sikh families.
